stem:
Nila looks at the diagram of $\triangle ABC$. Two interior angles are marked $58^{\circ}$ at $B$ and $47^{\circ}$ at $C$.

Which claim correctly finds the remaining interior angle at $A$?

options.text: Angle $A$ is $58^{\circ}$, because that is the parallel-line label for this triangle.
Angle $A$ is $180^{\circ}-(58^{\circ}+47^{\circ})=75^{\circ}$, using the other two interior angles of the same triangle.
Angle $A$ is $58^{\circ}+47^{\circ}=105^{\circ}$, treating the sum of the known angles as the missing one.
Use an exterior-angle supplement at a neighbouring polygon instead of the two interior angles of $\triangle ABC$.

teacher.key_rationale: Interior angles of a triangle sum to 180°, so A = 180° − (58° + 47°) = 75°. Calling A a parallel-line measure, adding instead of subtracting from 180°, or leaving the triangle for an exterior supplement miss the hinge.
teacher.figure_note: Rewrote source triangle ABC with interior angles 58° at B, 47° at C, and unknown at A.
